benchmarks.listening: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
benchmarks.speaking: Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
benchmarks.reading: Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
benchmarks.writing: Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
benchmarks.lengua: ~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.

benchmarks.listening: Understand short simple dialogues about family, school, animals, food (Cambridge Starters Listening parts 1–4).
benchmarks.speaking: Answer picture-prompted questions; describe a picture in simple sentences.
benchmarks.reading: Read 2–3-sentence texts; match pictures to words and short captions.
benchmarks.writing: Copy words and complete short sentences (Starters Reading/Writing parts).
benchmarks.lengua: ~450 words (Starters wordlist); Present simple, present continuous (limited), there is/are, like + -ing.

benchmarks.listening: Understand short dialogues with more vocabulary; identify main information in simple announcements.
benchmarks.speaking: Describe routines, favourites, community helpers; give short opinions.
benchmarks.reading: Read short paragraphs; answer simple comprehension Qs; find specific info.
benchmarks.writing: Write short paragraph about self/family/routine (40–70 words).
benchmarks.lengua: ~800 words; All basic tenses start; must/have to/could; SVA; superlatives.

benchmarks.listening: Understand longer dialogues (Movers parts 1–5); identify specific info in spoken texts.
benchmarks.speaking: Describe places, objects, past events; role-play simple situations.
benchmarks.reading: Read and sequence short stories; locate information in signs, notices.
benchmarks.writing: Write a note/message of 30–40 words (Movers Writing part); classroom paragraphs 60–100w.
benchmarks.lengua: ~1350 words (Movers wordlist); Past simple, relatives, infinitive of purpose, have to.

benchmarks.listening: Understand dialogues and short stories (Flyers parts 1–5); infer mood from intonation.
benchmarks.speaking: Narrate stories with past/present/future; express preferences with reasons.
benchmarks.reading: Read and understand short stories (80–250 words); find main idea and detail.
benchmarks.writing: Writing Part 3: 20–25-word picture story (Flyers); classroom pieces 100–150w.
benchmarks.lengua: ~2500 words (Flyers wordlist); Present perfect intro, tag Qs, 0th conditional, be going to.

benchmarks.listening: Follow dialogues and announcements (KET Listening parts 1–5); 25-minute exam.
benchmarks.speaking: KET Speaking: 2 parts, 8–10 min; interview + collaborative task.
benchmarks.reading: Understand signs, notices, emails, short articles (KET Reading parts 1–5).
benchmarks.lengua: ~1500 words (KET list); All basic tenses + present perfect, full modals.

benchmarks.listening: Follow longer dialogues (3–5 min) at B1 level; identify speakers' attitudes.
benchmarks.speaking: Sustain 3-minute discussions on familiar topics; reach agreement in pairs.
benchmarks.reading: Read articles, reports, narratives up to 450 words; infer meaning.
benchmarks.writing: Produce 100–150w emails, articles; basic report format.
benchmarks.lengua: ~2200 words; past perfect, conditionals 0-1-2, reported speech (statements).

benchmarks.listening: PET Listening: 4 parts, 30 min; multiple choice, gap fill, note-taking.
benchmarks.speaking: PET Speaking: 4 parts, 10–12 min; individual + paired collaborative.
benchmarks.reading: PET Reading: 6 parts; gapped text, multi-matching, multiple-choice cloze.
benchmarks.writing: PET Writing: Part 1 email ~100w; Part 2 article OR story ~100w.
benchmarks.lengua: ~3200 words (PET list); all tenses mastered, all conditionals, passive, reported.

benchmarks.listening: FCE Listening: 4 parts, 40 min; monologues, interviews, multi-task.
benchmarks.speaking: FCE Speaking: 4 parts, 14 min; interview, picture comparison, discussion.
benchmarks.reading: FCE Reading/Use of English: 7 parts, 75 min.
benchmarks.writing: FCE Writing: Part 1 essay 140–190w compulsory; Part 2 one of article/email/letter/report/review 140–190w.
benchmarks.lengua: ~4500 words; cond. 3 + mixed, passive all tenses, past modals, complex relatives.

benchmarks.listening: Comprehension of extended discourse; academic lecture excerpts.
benchmarks.speaking: Presentations 5–7 min; Q&A; justifying opinions with evidence.
benchmarks.writing: Persuasive / argumentative essays 400–500w; CV + cover letter.
benchmarks.lengua: ~5000 words; subjunctive, participle clauses, inversion (intro), cleft (intro).

benchmarks.listening: CAE Listening: 4 parts, 40 min; complex attitudes, inference.
benchmarks.speaking: CAE Speaking: 4 parts, 15 min; interview, long turn, collaborative, discussion.
benchmarks.reading: CAE Reading/UoE: 8 parts, 90 min; multi-matching, cross-text.
benchmarks.writing: CAE Writing: Part 1 essay 220–260w; Part 2 one of letter/email, proposal, report, review 220–260w.
benchmarks.lengua: ~5500–6000 words; inversion, cleft, nominalisation, impersonal passive, hedging.

calendario.actividad: Placement test + CEFR baseline to identify prep needs
Foundation + exam skills + familiarisation with formats
First mock: YLE + KET + PET + FCE + CAE — FULL OFFICIAL TIMING
Analyse results · identify weak skills · adjust teaching plan
Target weak skills · past papers · timing practice · vocabulary push
calendario.kpi: Past paper bank built · weekly progress

calendario.actividad: Speaking practice intensification · writing drills · listening in exam format
Second mock: final rehearsal under official conditions
Last-mile revision · enrol through Cambridge centre · parent briefing
Cambridge official exam day — all papers (speaking may be scheduled ±1 week)
Results analysis · individual student reports · parent communication · next-year plan
